% note: Post hoc reading on point estimates and stamped 95\% intervals: nothing is fitted and no frontier is drawn. Settings from different studies, puzzle sets and runs are compared only as our reading, not a test; each row names its study, set and label.
% note: Two blocks, named in the first column. In the first, a setting clears a target when its accuracy (the point estimate) is at or above the target; in the second, when the lower end of its 95\% interval is at or above the target. Each row gives the cheapest setting that clears the target at that length and shape, or says that no measured setting clears it (a dash stands for each number it then lacks). Where rounding would put a value on the target, one more decimal is printed.
% note: Candidates (every measured setting with a stamped accuracy, 95\% interval and list cost per answer at that length and shape): at 6 steps, Study~1's single-call settings and step voting (chains only), its Haiku-medium vote line ($k$~=~2 to 40) and Haiku-max's vote of $k$~=~3 samples; Study~1b's effort-sweep settings on the 6-step set and Haiku-max votes of $k$~=~2 to 10 (free analysis 2, post hoc); the top-up run's Haiku team, its picker (whose cost includes its samples) and its step voting (pieces only). At 16 steps, Study~1b's effort-sweep settings and its Haiku-max vote curve ($k$~=~2 to 10).
% note: Every vote row is estimated from the samples made per puzzle, not from separate runs of $k$ calls: Study~1b's Haiku-max votes from 10 samples per puzzle on the 6-step set and 10 on the 16-step set (the expected accuracy of a vote of $k$ of them, a tie credited as a share split evenly among the tied answers); Study~1's Haiku-max vote from its 3 samples and its Haiku-medium vote line from 40. A vote's list cost per answer is $k$ times one sample's.
% note: Lower ends are those of the stamped 95\% intervals over puzzles, as each setting's file stamps them: Clopper--Pearson (exact) for the Opus and Sonnet settings with one sample per puzzle; cluster bootstrap for every other setting (the Haiku settings, Study~1b's Opus-medium, step voting, the top-up designs and every vote); Clopper--Pearson from free analysis 4 (post hoc) where a bootstrap interval collapsed to one value. Every lower end printed in this table is that of a cluster bootstrap.
% note: Format compliance is the share of answered samples in the required format; for a vote, that of the samples it is drawn from.
% note: Where a candidate's bootstrap interval collapsed to one value, its lower end is that of the exact (Clopper--Pearson) 95\% interval from free analysis 4 (post hoc) over the same puzzles, so no candidate is left out of the lower-end ranking. That holds for 6 candidates: Haiku-max vote, $k$~=~3, on chains (Study~1, main set; Study~1, exploratory setting): accuracy 100.00\%, lower end 95.49\% (exact, post hoc; 80 puzzles); Haiku-max vote, $k$~=~9, on chains (Study~1b, 6-step set; post hoc (free analysis 2)): accuracy 100.00\%, lower end 91.19\% (exact, post hoc; 40 puzzles); Haiku-max vote, $k$~=~10, on chains (Study~1b, 6-step set; post hoc (free analysis 2)): accuracy 100.00\%, lower end 91.19\% (exact, post hoc; 40 puzzles); Opus-medium, one sample, on pieces (Study~1b, 6-step set; Study~1b, pre-specified descriptive (effort sweep)): accuracy 100.00\%, lower end 91.19\% (exact, post hoc; 40 puzzles); Haiku, thinking off, one sample, on chains (Study~1b, 16-step set; Study~1b, pre-specified descriptive (effort sweep)): accuracy 0.00\%, lower end 0.00\% (exact, post hoc; 80 puzzles); Haiku-max vote, $k$~=~10, on pieces (Study~1b, 16-step set; Study~1b, pre-specified descriptive (vote curve)): accuracy 100.00\%, lower end 95.49\% (exact, post hoc; 80 puzzles).
